transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
JPMorgan Chase suffered an outage Monday that affected customers at the country's biggest lender,
but a spokesperson later said transactions were back to normal by Monday evening.
NPR's Rafael Naum reports.
Chase blamed an incident on a software bug and said it was not cyberrelated.
Earlier, some customers had complained about being unable to use Chase ATMs
or conduct some online transactions.
The bug also affected other banks and their customers,
impacting things like money transfers from Chase to other lenders.
The incident is the latest tech failure to hit the U.S.
Last week, Microsoft reported a major outage,
while the Federal Aviation Administration said an issue with old equipment led to widespread flight disruptions.
Also on Monday, United Airlines temporarily delayed some flights after suffering its own system outage.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
Before leaving for a trip to Asia, President Trump spoke to reporters Monday morning.
He was asked why he did not issue a statement about Friday's nationwide ground stop.
I was in the White House, as you know. I was in the White House on Saturday and Friday,
having meetings with Secretary Duffy and with everybody involved.
And I didn't think there was any reason for me to do it. I thought they did a very good job.
Trump said he does not take any responsibility for the ground stop,
blaming it instead on old technology and the Biden administration.
Trump is due to arrive in the Philippines in a few hours of first stop of his Asia trip.
Then it's on to China, where he used to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
Trump said Monday that he may also meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.
The Trump administration, taking new steps, prevent China from gaining access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers.
The new rule announced by the Commerce Department Monday seeks to close a loophole
that allows China to remotely access American AI technology.
California is suing OpenAI following an attack over the summer by the company's AI agents
on software company Hugging Face, and Piers Wojing-Wong reports.
In the complaint, California alleges that OpenAI has understated how unsafe its products are.
It says the company has admitted that "it lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing."
That's a number higher than previously reported.
Drawing from OpenAI's own reports about the Hugging Face attack,
California alleges that the top AI company has engaged in unfair competition and created a public nuisance.
It asked the court to stop such activities and order the company to pay damages in an amount yet to be determined.
In response, OpenAI said that the lawsuit singles it out for industry-wide challenges
and that it's committed to work with the state on improving safety practices.
Wojinan, NPR News.
This is NPR. A third U.S. aircraft carrier arriving in the Middle East, U.S. Central Command said in a social media post Monday
that the USS Theodore Roosevelt has entered its area of operations, bringing thousands of additional troops amid stalled talks with Iran.
Roosevelt, with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September.
Vice President J.D. Vance says he will decide sometime next year whether to seek the presidency.
Vance was asked about a potential 2028 presidential bid during an appearance on Fox News.
He said he's not yet made a decision, but he'll figure that out next year.
The Best New Artist category at the Grammys recognizes artists who have made a major breakthrough in their careers.
This year's nominees range from country to rap and indie rock.
Here's NPR's Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento.
There are eight artists in the running for Best New Artist.
On the alternative side, there's the Brooklyn rock band East and the mask-wearing math rock duo Angène de Portrine.
Country singer Ella Langley, electro pop star Slater, and the quirky pop funk of Remy Wolf also got nods.
So did the rapper Don Toliver.
And for fans of a throwback soul and R&B sound, there's English singer Sienna Spiro and a girl group formed by the granddaughters of Sam Cooke.
They are the Woolmax sisters.
All eight acts will compete for Best New Artist at the Grammy ceremony in February.
Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento, NPR News.
And I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.

topics.text: JPMorgan Chase outage from a software bug affects ATMs, online transactions, and interbank transfers
Trump says he took no responsibility for Friday's nationwide ground stop, blames old technology
Trump departs for Asia trip, first stop in the Philippines, with possible meeting with Kim Jong-un
Trump administration rule blocks China's remote access to advanced U.S. AI computing chips and servers
California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face attack, alleging unsafe AI agents and unfair competition
USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group enters Middle East as Iran talks stall
Vice President J.D. Vance says he will decide next year whether to seek the presidency
Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento previews eight Best New Artist Grammy nominees across genres
